quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks and obey all signs and signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicycles.

questions.question: You must use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: He or she is deaf.
He or she is a police officer.
He or she is blind.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right of way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: When another car's headlights are blinding you, you should:

options.text: Use your high beams until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming car has its high beams on, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: Your blind spot is an area you:

options.text: Cannot see without turning your head.
Can see directly behind your vehicle.
Can see in your rearview mirror.
Can see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas next to and behind your vehicle that you cannot see without turning your head.

questions.question: Traffic signals may show arrows to control turns from certain lanes. A green arrow means:

options.text: It is only used on one-way streets.
You may proceed, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may only proceed if there is also a circular green light.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may proceed, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go, but you must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Traffic signal.
Fire station.
T intersection.
Left turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal.
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells you a traffic signal is coming. It is yellow with black markings. Be ready to stop for a red light or deal with cross traffic.

questions.question: When you see an accident, you should:

options.text: Keep focusing on your own driving.
Keep moving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not stop just to look.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Always drives slowly.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at the same speed at all times.
Only drives in areas they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: Any driver can get distracted. A defensive driver watches other drivers and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: Drivers cannot pass across a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down, but don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren nearby but don't know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not heading toward you.

questions.question: What should you do if you see an animal on the road?

options.text: No special action is needed.
Honk your horn.
Pass the animal as closely as possible.
Be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Always be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid startling or scaring it.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect your driving ability. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces your focus on driving. It is better to wait to drive than to risk driving when you are emotionally upset.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain has stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain causes oil in the road to rise to the surface. This is worse in hot weather because heat causes even more oil to come to the surface.

questions.question: You see the driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Give the vehicle extra space.
Know that the driver is not paying full attention to the road.
Don't copy the driver's bad habits.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay focused while driving. Don't look at passengers, search for items, or daydream. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because accidents are more likely.

questions.question: When a funeral procession is on the road, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Another driver
A pedestrian
The funeral procession
A bicyclist

questions.correctAnswerText: The funeral procession
questions.explanation: All drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must let funeral processions pass. When the first vehicle enters an intersection, all other vehicles in the procession can follow through, even if traffic lights or signs say to stop.

questions.question: What is the safest way to drive in traffic?

options.text: Change your speed to stay alert.
Drive faster than the flow of traffic.
Drive slower than the flow of traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Always drive with the flow of traffic while staying within the speed limit.

questions.question: An aggressive driver is behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as he or she passes you.
Speed up as he or she is passing you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: When you meet an aggressive driver, move out of their way. Don't make eye contact with them. Speeding up may anger them more and make them more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign shape and color mean?

options.text: No passing zone
Wrong way
Railroad crossing
Stop

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs only mean one thing: no passing zone.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road meets a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road meets a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign means your road intersects with a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the oncoming traffic lane to complete your pass. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you:

options.text: Must drive slowly so approaching vehicles and pedestrians have time to move.
Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to move.
Must stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians crossing. Stop before crossing the sidewalk area. Failing to stop is against the law.

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is divided by ____ lines.

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if no other traffic is crossing.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are used at dangerous intersections. Treat them the same way you treat stop signs.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
Exiting an expressway.
Following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Keep driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles already in the intersection. You may continue, but drive at a speed that lets you slow down or stop if the light changes before you reach it.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Always yield to pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Use different routes.
Drive the same as you would on dry roads.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase your following distance. Your vehicle will take longer to stop than it would on dry roads.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle by law?

options.text: Anyone under 18 years old
Adult passengers
The driver
Backseat passengers

questions.correctAnswerText: Anyone under 18 years old
questions.explanation: Seat belts prevent injury and death in crashes. Anyone under 18 must wear a seat belt by law. However, everyone should wear a seat belt regardless of age.

questions.question: You are in an accident and someone is injured. You should:

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move the injured unless necessary. Moving them incorrectly can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they may look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they may look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they look drunk. Coffee, open windows, and loud radio are not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert to dangers on the road.

questions.question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
You have the right-of-way.
Force your way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will change lanes for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering an interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when you have an opening.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both the inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before every lane change, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spots.

questions.question: When can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or possess alcohol in any vehicle on a public road or sidewalk. You cannot have an open container of alcohol in any part of the vehicle where people sit, no matter where you are in the vehicle.

questions.question: How can you prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas and let your vehicle slow before braking.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. When stopping, release the accelerator first to slow down, then apply steady brake pressure. This activates your brake lights and stops your vehicle smoothly.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians are walking along the road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians cannot cross here.
Construction workers are on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a pedestrian crossing is ahead. Be careful and watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: If a car's high beams are coming toward you, where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road
The center of the road
The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: If an oncoming car is using high beams, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your lane until the car passes.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Keep your tires at the correct air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your car slides on water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase this risk. Speeding also increases the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What should you do with loose objects in your vehicle?

options.text: Place them on the back seat.
Place them on the dashboard.
Secure them so they do not become hazards.
Keep them on the back shelf.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure them so they do not become hazards.
questions.explanation: In a crash, loose objects can fly around and injure people in the vehicle. Do not place heavy or sharp objects on the dashboard or rear shelf.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right if there is an open right lane.
If there is no right lane, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear to encourage them to pass.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If being tailgated and a right lane is open, move over. If not, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear. This encourages the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.
